headline: No shared execution or data channels: prompt-injection, leakage, and capability-conflict risks are effectively blocked; only low compliance ambiguity remains.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable knowledge-management artifact with no I/O surfaces, and agent B is documentation-only with no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, or MCP. There is no documented channel for A’s content to reach B as executable instructions, so prompt injection is not plausible in this pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP server, reassess injection risk.
IF B begins parsing A’s content as instructions rather than reference text, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents disconnected from shared channels.
Require manual copy/paste only for any cross-agent transfer.
Document that A’s outputs are reference-only, not instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has network egress none; B also touches no data classes and has no filesystem, clipboard, or API surfaces. With no shared workspace or outbound path, there is no plausible leakage route between the two agents.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to sensitive files or a shared workspace, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF B gains API or filesystem access, data exfiltration pathways may appear.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of both agents’ environments.
Do not mount a shared workspace.
Verify B remains fileless and API-less before deployment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is not runnable and exposes no write or network capabilities; B explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use MCP. Because neither agent can mutate a shared resource, there is no capability overlap that could create write conflicts.
conditions: IF A becomes runnable with write or network permissions, conflict analysis must be repeated.
IF B is granted filesystem or git write access, shared-resource contention may emerge.
mitigations: Avoid assigning both agents to the same mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a reference list and B is a content-writing cheat sheet, so B may use A as source material if an operator manually transfers content. However, B has no autonomous action-taking surfaces, and A is not generating operational facts; the main risk is mistaken reuse of reference text, not downstream harm.
conditions: IF an operator copies A’s entries into B as authoritative facts, B may propagate errors.
IF B is later connected to publishing or action-taking tools, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Require human review of any copied content.
Label A as a reference source, not an authority.
Use a checklist to verify citations before publication.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, with no data classes touched and no declared sensitive-data handling. The only compliance concern is residual ambiguity about residency, retention, or certification because neither profile documents those controls; this is a documentation gap rather than an active breach.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data, residency and retention controls must be documented.
IF a jurisdictional or certification requirement is introduced, the current profiles are insufficient.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data until controls are documented.
Add a compliance owner review before rollout.
